title: Circuit Builder
intro: Build a closed loop with a battery, a wire, a switch and an LED. Open the loop and see what happens. Add the switch and use it to turn the light on and off.
note: This is a model of the lesson's circuits that uses the lesson's own tester data; it skips how much energy one cell has, so the LED and doorbell run from one cell. The real build in the lesson (foil path, LED, paper-clip switch, light-up card) still counts. Safety in the real build: an adult hands out and collects every cell, tape cells when stored, a swallowed coin cell is a medical emergency, never use wall electricity, and unhook anything that feels warm.
summary: Current flows only in a closed loop. A gap, an open switch or an insulator breaks the path; metals conduct; an LED lights only one way. In every working circuit, electrical energy changes into something useful — light, a little heat, or sound.

rounds.goal: Make the LED light. Fill every slot so the loop has no gaps. One piece in the tray does not belong.
rounds.done: The LED lights: electrical energy changed into light and a little heat.

rounds.goal: Build the loop with the switch. The switch starts open, and there is a spare wire. Find out what the switch does.
rounds.done: Switch closed: the path is complete and the LED lights. Switch open: the path is broken. A flashlight works exactly this way.

rounds.goal: One slot is a test gap. Put each material in the gap and watch the LED. Test all five.
rounds.done: The metals conducted — the paper clip and the foil lit the LED. String, plastic and wood are insulators. That is why a wire is metal inside a plastic coat.

rounds.goal: Run the LED and the doorbell at the same time. There are two switches, and not every piece belongs in the loop.
rounds.done: The LED lights and the doorbell rings: electrical energy changed into light and sound at the same time. Both switches had to be closed.
